items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: Eddie Grochet and Huntsnagle... Manuel had his band on there, Joe had his band, see, well, because we used to work, we were the Superior band, see, when Superior band go, off on gigs, we work in there... Superior band and the McNally band worked for Huntsnagle

ctx.x: Well they're sitting in back here.

They're flying. No, he wouldn't leave New Orleans. That's how they got Joe Howard on the boat. But you're talking way before the people left. I'm talking, I'm going when we first started on the boat, see. They had Frank Duesen. Oh, gee. That's how they did. Yeah, we were first on the boat. Frank Duesen. They had a guy called James Alexander, drummer. And Manuel come on there for a while, Manuel Perez. Correct. Then we had Andrew Kimberl for a while, see. On trumpet, yeah. On trumpet, see. Then our clients were…

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: And I went down to this big chief, big Indian trombone player.

ctx.x: Is that backstage in the Paramount Theater? Yeah, that's backstage in the Paramount Theater, yeah. Yeah, with Bud Freeman. Yeah, I've seen that. Only it's a different shot, I think. The other one Louie was playing, I think.

Always wearing glasses. This is a little bit of sketchy. Now, this is when Papa Sutterstatt come up here to visit the player of the date up here, this big chief trombone player, this big Indian chief. Who was that? That was at the Metro Bowl. Oh, in New York. New York, see? Oh, I didn't remember. See, Papa Sutterstatt, see? And this is a good friend. He was staying at my house when he come up here. Uh-huh. See? And I went down to this big chief, big Indian trombone player.
Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. He was the last I heard him, uh...
